column3: 790-line release history; records the 1.0.0 removal of the whole harness (sessions, storage, compaction, skills) from this package, leaving only Agent + the loop, and the shouldStopAfterTurn->finishTurn migration with its error/aborted guard.
50-line example wiring an Agent to an MCP server: one AgentTool per MCP tool plus a codemode tool whose scripts call them.

172 lines: createMcpTools maps MCP tools to AgentTools (name sanitised to 64 chars of [A-Za-z0-9_-], input schema forced to {type:object,properties}); createNestedToolRunner bridges a tool calling a tool through runToolCall so beforeToolCall/afterToolCall still apply.
Manifest for @earendil-works/pi-agent-core v1.4.0; runtime deps are only pi-ai and typebox, Node >= 22.19.0.

569-line user doc: the event-sequence diagrams, the two queues, the four hooks (transformContext/convertToLlm/prepareRequest/prepareNextTurn/finishTurn) and the rule that raw agentLoop() streams are observational while the Agent class is a barrier.

The turn engine (959 lines): outer/inner loop, declareToolChanges diffing executable vs declared tools, length-truncated tool calls refused, terminate unanimity, parallel tool execution emitting completion-order events but source-order results, runToolCall for nested calls.

Stateful Agent wrapper (623 lines): PendingMessageQueue with all/one-at-a-time modes, the state reducer over events, awaited listeners in order, thrown failures turned into a full synthetic event sequence, reset() refusing during an active run.
5-line barrel re-exporting agent.ts, agent-loop.ts, proxy.ts, types.ts and only setDefaultStreamFn from stream-fn.ts.
streamProxy(): a StreamFn that talks to a server, reconstructing the partial message from a reduced event vocabulary; a clean EOF without a terminal event becomes an error rather than a hang.
20-line holder for the fallback StreamFn so pi-agent-core need not depend on a provider catalog; getDefaultStreamFn throws with a message naming both escapes.
Every type in the package: the AgentLoopConfig hook surface, the 10-event AgentEvent vocabulary, AgentTool/AgentToolResult, AgentState, and AgentMessage opened for declaration merging.

2234 lines, the behavioural spec of the loop: event-sequence assertions, length-truncation refusal, completion-order vs source-order tool results, finishTurn ordering and its three satisfiability cases, the terminate-unanimity rule and runToolCall's exact hook order.

1229 lines, the spec of the Agent wrapper: the tool-loadout announcement sequence, executable-set-wins rewrite, full event sequence on a thrown provider error, awaited agent_end listeners, reset() during a run, and queues preserved on error/end.

416 lines, the only e2e test: the real streamSimple against the faux provider, asserting transcript shape, pendingToolCalls at the exact start/end events, abort leaving stopReason 'aborted', and thinking blocks preserved in order.
118 lines: three regressions for streamProxy (toolcall_end-only metadata preserved, a non-newline-terminated terminal event processed, a stream without a terminal event surfacing as an error).
Fixture tool 'calculate' evaluating an expression via new Function, plus a variant that attaches a Usage to the result.
Fixture tool 'get_current_time' with an optional IANA timezone; an invalid timezone throws a message that still states the current UTC time.
Three-line helper: waitForTick() = setTimeout 0, used to let queued turns settle in tests.
13-line build config with rootDir src, include src/**/*.ts and paths mapping pi-ai to the sibling package's dist; tests and examples are excluded by construction.
27-line vitest config: 30s timeout, silent passed-only, and resolve.alias mapping pi-ai, pi-ai/compat, pi-agent-core and pi-telemetry to SOURCE files so tests run against source.

19.7KB release history; the richest source of why. Records the 1.3.0 vocabulary migration (Handle->Ref, epoch->codeVersion, kind->variant, eager->lifetime), the 1.4.0 fix list (loader duplicates, dead links, early retirement, disposed objects staying reachable, AbortSignal.any keeping a code generation alive, EPIPE crash), and a measured 11.3s->1.4s array-append fix.

814-line usage guide read from line 580 (Plugins, Hot reload, Hosts and links, Durable, the error table and the Rules of thumb) plus the full heading map; the rules-of-thumb table encodes the engineering policy.

288-line specification read in full: concepts, contracts, the compatibility rule, factory/declaration semantics, activation, lifetime, roots/code versions, the reload protocol, flow control, and a 'Still open' list of nine named holes plus a Decisions list.
931-line tutorial read via its heading map plus the closing habits/checklist (lines 835-904); every printed example is fenced with example markers and compared to a runnable test source.
Manifest for @earendil-works/chord v1.4.0: one runtime dep (pi-telemetry) plus typebox, and nine subpath exports each carrying a 'source' condition.
202-line README: the entry-point table, quick start, telemetry sections, and the delta section restating the ownership contract (callers must not mutate transferred or published data).

402 lines: the Cell (tracked box {v:value}, unboxed ops) and Derived (synchronous projection); writes publish only mutated paths, replace() diffs when containers are shared, dependents are recomputed and validated before publication, and everything publishes inside holdPublications().

251 lines: the cross-host reload protocol - the server retires first so its retire frames precede prepare, collects votes with a deadline, commits or aborts everywhere, and reconcileChild() brings a late child up to the parent's code version.

1327 lines: one link's protocol - frame dispatch, the RelayRef, the flow-control window (256 KiB, 4 windows cap), lazy unit slots, lazy state slots that become resets, and maxCalls answered with unavailable/too_many_calls.

161 lines: the explicit Context - typed values, cancellation (withAbortSignal combines via AbortSignal.any, withoutAbortSignal masks it for cleanup) and required telemetry, with no AsyncLocalStorage dependency.

440 lines: the contract system - remote/local/method/opaque, placement resolution, description+fingerprint, and coverage()/bind() structural compatibility (a moved type is never bridged by an adapter).
38 lines: the shapes a factory declares besides state cells - ResourceDeclaration (version/deps/exclusive/open/close), Resource, ListenerDecl and the ValueOf/EventOf type helpers.
128 lines: a fast applier for self-produced ops with no validation, copying each touched container once via a shared mutable DATA_DESCRIPTOR.

523 lines: structural diff between two JSON revisions - string append/overlap-truncate, positional then identity then LCS array matching, permutation ops, and an economic final decision comparing the delta's encoded cost against a whole snapshot.
10 lines: the Draft<T> type, a deeply-mutable view of a JSON value with recursion capped at depth 8.

738 lines: the delta public surface - the Op/WireOp vocabularies, RESERVED_SEGMENTS path safety, assertIndexInRange (sparse arrays and a 4.29-billion-entry DoS), the appliers, and the encoder/decoder (path interning on second use, a base op clearing both dictionaries as a recovery point).

193-line delta specification: the mutation-rights table, the ownership contract (nothing is frozen; an illegal mutation silently corrupts), the undefined rules by position, the op table, and measured costs (19 ms / 20 MiB for a 100k unshift; 9 ms vs 0.08 ms for 20k nested reads).

75 lines: JsonRevisionValidator validates a revision is strict JSON (dense arrays, plain objects, enumerable data properties, no cycles/symbols) while skipping containers already validated in an earlier revision via a WeakSet.

2239 lines (read in 5 targeted windows plus the full symbol map, not every line): the Proxy-based mutable overlay, prepare/adopt as an infallible pointer swap, O(1) staling of competing contexts, depth-bucketed op emission with a 4096-op fold to a root replacement, the piece-tree array model and the ordered/element array plans. The array-mutator emulation block was read at its signatures only.

76 lines: 12 error codes, a finer free-form reason, a retryable set containing only superseded and upgrade_conflict, asChordError (keeps a known code, demotes the rest to unavailable with the cause) and runAll (every step, then one error or an AggregateError).

1300+ lines (read lines 1-260 plus the full symbol map, not every line): createHost/HostImpl, the required self and principalKey, two code versions (current+previous), facets with an aborting signal, registries, roots, connect/accept/route, and wave disposal (referrers before referents). The HostImpl body was not read line by line.
82-line package barrel re-exporting the contract API, createHost/defineFacet, the Draft type, the error helpers, the link builders, the replicatedState family, acceptWebSockets and PROTOCOL_VERSION.

135 lines: JsonValue, JsonRepresentation<T>, copyJson (whose copy walk IS the validator - rejecting cycles, non-plain prototypes, accessors, symbols, sparse arrays, non-finite numbers) and isJsonValue.

415 lines: the transports (memory with a sever() that simulates a dead network, Node IPC, WebSocket) plus the payload packing layer - a deflated payload kept as received, a binary WebSocket message layout, and send() returning the encoded size so a size-less link is not windowed.

67 lines: the Node facet loader - a registerHooks resolve hook carrying a cache-busting query into a facet's directory, every root registered before any import. Its own TODO states the leak: fresh module copies are never evicted and TUI plugins need isolation.

443 lines: forkDriver (detached so the whole process group can be killed), createHostManager (serialised start/stop/replace, shutdown grace, liveness/idle), childControl, and processLock - a kernel-owned lock (abstract socket / named pipe / probed socket file) with a 104-byte sun_path fallback.
16-line Node-only barrel: nodeLoader plus the host-manager surface.

1932 lines (read lines 1-360 plus the full symbol map, not every line): the Service/Factory/Lifetime model, the Self declaration surface with its per-kind reload survival rules, ResourceImpl (an open that completes after abort closes its value), ResourceFacade (value throws not_ready inside any factory), Decls and the HostCore interface. The ObjectImpl body was not read line by line.

406 lines: OutputBuffer (head/tail window, exact dropped byte/line totals for the whole stream, a skipped marker legal only with tail retention), boundOutput, sanitizeOutput, utf8ByteLength and Progress (adaptive commits paced at 100 KiB/s with at most one in flight).

39 lines: one process-wide FIFO queue for every observer notification, so a re-entrant write cannot overtake the write being published; holdPublications defers delivery until a multi-step change completes.
30 lines: defineRegistry with conflict error|last, a per-code-version RegistryTable and a RegistryView that notifies on every new table.

723 lines (read lines 1-350 plus the symbol map): the hot-reload protocol - load, checkProviders (a same-version contract must still cover the old description), prepare with the host.gating flag that closes the candidate set, dryRun validation of every prospective value, #stage subscribing listeners to catch failures in prepare, waitForRetirement aborting old roots before closing their resources, and commit/rollback.

658 lines (read lines 1-400): RemoteBinding - one hold per host+key shared by every reference, a shape applied only once all its snapshots are present, a state error before the first hydration ending the binding, detached() keeping last values readable after a link loss, and calls sending only what the consumer's schema knows.
219 lines: canonicalJson, a two-lane FNV hash64, assertValid/normalize/canonicalIdentity, and fits() - conservative structural subtyping where any unmodelled keyword forces exact equality.
5.8KB: the Durable Object SQLite adapter over a structural DurableObjectSqliteStorage binding; get() reads only the cursor's first row and a bigint outside the safe-integer range is refused.

38 lines: the portable SqliteExecutor/SqliteDatabase interfaces; the transaction contract is spelled out in the type (handle invalid after settle, rollback before rejecting, AggregateError if rollback also fails).
Three-line barrel: the database types, applySqliteMigrations and validateSqliteSchemaPrefix.
43 lines: applySqliteMigrations applies pending migrations in one transaction, refuses a stored version newer than supported, and checks version contiguity before touching the database.

201 lines: the Node adapter - a SerialOperationQueue that publishes its barrier before an operation starts, BEGIN IMMEDIATE transactions that AggregateError on rollback failure, and close() that checkpoints the WAL first.
9 lines: validateSqliteSchemaPrefix requires a valid identifier that does not start with the reserved sqlite_.

423 lines: replicatedState - atomic change (a throwing callback leaves the value and sequence unchanged and revokes the escaped draft), sync-only callbacks, no re-entrancy, a 100-frame per-subscription delivery cap that may skip, a contiguous source cursor, and errors rethrown in a microtask when no onError is given.

12KB: createSqliteTelemetry - a buffered portable recorder that performs no SQL on the recording path, flushes settled spans and ten-second metric aggregates in one transaction per second, bounds the queue at 10k settled spans, and stops recording permanently on a write failure.

171 lines: the read side - getTrace, findTraces with JSON cursor pagination inside one transaction, and findMetrics; the attribute filter distinguishes boolean true from numeric 1 via json_each's entry.type.
89 lines: the shared vocabulary - Ctx, GetOptions, Readable, StateEvent (snap|ops|reset), RefBase, Shape and RefStatus (including 'loading' again after a reconnect).

35 lines: acceptWebSockets wraps the socket at once (so frames sent during authentication are queued), deflates outgoing payloads and refuses packed frames from clients; WebSocket peers are always clients.

181 lines: the wire protocol - one TypeBox schema per frame type, isFrame() validation, PROTOCOL_VERSION 4 announced in hello (peers of different versions do not talk), payloads left as unknown and validated against the contract where used.

4 tests: an aborted get releases only its own reference while the binding stays, a ctx.get still waiting when its call settles rejects aborted, a get times out with unavailable/ready_timeout, and a ctx.get resolves hydrated with its reference released at the end of the call.

17.3KB: shared bindings - N references cost one hold, one snapshot per member, one frame per change and one release; lingering; the identity key; hydration over a link; method-only references; client-hold origins; protocol version 4 refusing a version-3 peer.

One test that scans every src/**/*.ts import specifier and fails if the package depends on any Pi package other than pi-telemetry or on any file outside src - a static dependency gate written as a test.

25.4KB: cross-host reload - every host prepares and the server commits first, a failing vote aborts every host, a worker gate past its deadline aborts the reload, facets are removed and tombstones reconciled, browsers are not participants, and a child that says hello during a reload is reconciled after it.

7 tests: distinct empty roots, layered typed values without modifying parents, inherited vs isolated cancellation, the cancellation mask, telemetry derived independently of values and cancellation, concurrent traceIn branches, and awaitWithContext stopping on cancellation.

7 tests: input normalisation and default-omitting identity, stable description-based fingerprints, reserved member names and opaque remote members, coverage of additive vs breaking changes, methods with and without args/result, binding across versions only through accepts, and opaque/function member comparison.

11.2KB: the checked applier - each touched container copied once, root-replacement payloads protected from later edits, one copy-on-write scope across batch partitions, tracker-produced batches across arbitrary revision boundaries, no partial application on failure, and one batch fanning out without mutating shared payloads.
5.5KB: a spawn-per-scenario harness over 18 scenarios (import, committed-read, draft-read, sparse, queue, sort, dense, unshift and the watch-* replication family), writing results to a temp file.
15KB: the worker's implementation of those 18 scenarios, measuring the tracker against a control for both reads and replication.

9.7KB: a conversation-view-shaped benchmark (provisional pico5 schema) with projection-control, normal, fanout, delayed-start-lag, churn-reconnect, overflow-reset and branch-head-replacement, timing mutation/prepare/adopt/synthesize/projectApply separately.

39KB: the conversation-view worker - a five-key mounted document (config, inbox, turn, preferences, live) plus an audit document, driven through mutation, prepare, adopt, synthesize and project-apply.
4.4KB: a memory harness with idle-control, sparse-burst, staggered-revisions and lagging-watches, reporting work/acquisition time, GC count and time, ready heap/RSS and peak-over-ready deltas.
6.1KB: the memory worker - a 100k-row document with N watches and M updates, reporting GC counts, heap deltas and a final checksum so a measurement cannot silently drift.

4 tests: the tracker takes O(1) ownership of the imported revision without traversing it (a root with a throwing getter is never read), null prototypes are preserved, and assigned/inserted values are copied immediately.

10.8KB: the diff - sets/deletes, string append and front truncation, array splices, a same-length queue collapsing to two splices, a pure reorder as a permutation, deeply-equal reorders normalising to a no-op, permutation validation, narrowness assertions at 256 KiB / 1 MiB / 1 001 / 10 000 / 40 000 items, and wide-object/array fallbacks to a root replacement.
992 bytes: spawns retention.worker.ts with --expose-gc for 14 named scenarios and asserts a clean exit - a memory-leak gate expressed as a test.
11.9KB: builds a WeakRef to a large payload inside a draft, settles the change in various ways, forces GC up to 30 times and asserts the payload was collected.

58KB: the tracker's behavioural spec in six groups - transactional lifecycle, policy view (native reads, key ordering, coercion, one proxy identity per container), by-value placements, piece arrays (one insert for a long-array append, removals from the end backwards, permutations, 20 000-op queue -> two ops), a seeded 100-step randomised convergence check, and prototype-pollution safety.
6.8KB: a cold/full traversal benchmark comparing raw, proxy and delta access over a drawing document, with a 4-job GC settle before sampling; the delta README quotes its numbers.

17.9KB: the delta module's spec - tracker lifecycle, canonical strings and bounded overlaps, operation application and validation, the codec (path interning, adjacent-path omission, base resets the dictionary, self-contained batches after a base), ownership, path/prototype safety, array index safety and operation structure safety.
2.2KB: a link wrapper that records every frame sent and received, counts frames by type and extracts the state frames.
327 bytes: a single Echo remote contract with one echo method, used by the host-manager tests.

3.6KB: runs the Node facet loader OUTSIDE vitest (its module runner bypasses the resolve hooks), writing a temporary plugin, reloading it after editing a relative import, and checking cross-facet module sharing.
1.5KB: a child host for the manager tests; FIXTURE_MODE selects normal/ignore-shutdown/fatal, it takes the kernel lock before owning data, spawns a grandchild to test tree-killing and reports ready.

10.5KB: flow control with units - a new get resolves at once behind a full window, a snapshot larger than the window arrives whole, a size-less (IPC) link never holds state back, waiting ops stay under the per-link cap and each then gets one reset, and a stalled tab overflows while another keeps every change.

10.3KB: the flow-control core - state waits while the window is full while calls are answered, ops that outgrow their slot become the current value, what waits for a released reference is dropped, relayed state is coalesced, a peer without acks is neither windowed nor acknowledged, and maxCalls answers beyond the limit with too_many_calls.

6.5KB: a GC gate using v8 --expose-gc and a FinalizationRegistry - a reference held across six reloads keeps only the current generation, a lifetime:host object's state/resource/listener/task/registrations do not keep an old one, and abort listeners on ctx.signal do not outlive their call or task.

11.7KB: the host's own reference to a lifetime:host object follows contract bumps at commit without reopening it, old-version consumers still refuse an upgrade without accepts, object-owned old references block an upgrade, a forgotten bump stays refused, a cluster upgrade re-tokens only after unanimous preparation, and a lifetime change creates or releases the host object.
24.5KB: the host's own behaviour - serving, factories, principals, variants, references, registries, lifetime and disposal.

6.5KB: hydration as an activation precondition - an object forwarding and deriving from a remote member goes live with its value, a member read inside a factory throws not_ready, a child's host object goes live once the parent admits it, and a cross-host reference cycle fails at readyTimeout with a cycle hint.

2.7KB: isJsonValue and copyJson - strict-JSON checks, alias-free copying, omitUndefinedProperties (objects only), null prototypes and an own __proto__ data property preserved, and rejection of cycles, sparse arrays, extra keys, subclasses, accessors, hidden properties and symbols.
24KB: the link layer - memory/IPC/WebSocket transports, the packed-payload path (Packed/unpack), frame-level behaviour and the PROTOCOL_VERSION handshake.
19.3KB: regression tests for a phase-1b review's findings #1-#11 and the shared-worker test gap, with a WatchedLink that can close on a chosen frame to simulate a mid-conversation drop.
857 bytes: spawns test/fixtures/loader.ts as a child process (vitest's module runner bypasses the loader's resolve hooks) and asserts a clean exit.
7.4KB: the host manager - serialised start/stop/replace, a child that exits before ready, a fatal child, the shutdown grace and process-group kill, the kernel lock, and liveness/idle reporting.

5.4KB: a property test - 3000 seeded random streams assert that a buffer receiving skipped markers produces the SAME snapshot as the full stream for every legal skip pattern, plus exact dropped byte/line counting and the refusal of skips under head retention.
12.3KB: boundOutput, OutputBuffer and Progress - the tail bound compared byte-for-byte against Buffer's own tail slice across every byte limit including multi-byte characters.

8.5KB: placement - a get goes where the contract places the input and the caller never names a host, serve refuses a type the host is not the place of, a host refuses a hold its contract places elsewhere, the host comes from the normalised input, a moved type is never bridged by an adapter, and the compile-time hostFamily rules.

4.8KB: the principal model - typed narrowing in factories/methods/contexts, the host's own principal recognised by key (never invalidated), a child's parent acting as the principal given to connect while relayed callers keep theirs, and the refusal to create a host, connect or route without a principal.
3.1KB: with a vi.mock counting encoder()/encode(), one change to K clients costs K encodes (one per feed), no new streams, one frame per link and the SAME ops on every link.

7.1KB: startup readiness - install/load await resource activation and registration while lazy objects stay lazy, an eager factory/dependency/resource failure rejects with the same error object and reaches onError, load installs every facet first, a missing dependency rejects with unavailable/unknown_type, and awaitHostObjects:false defers eager readiness until the parent admits the worker.

24.8KB: hot reload - compatible changes without waiting, prepare isolation (writes throw; a failing factory leaves everything unchanged), a state version bump with migrate and the gate, upgrade_conflict for late old roots, the deadline abort, exclusive resource replacement, cross-host commit ordering, and two-version retirement with superseded.

8.9KB: public delivery for both the mutable and attached state - hydration and updates awaited independently per subscriber, the 100-delivery cap keeping only the newest, unsubscribe discarding pending work without aborting or joining a running callback, and failures reported in isolation.

13.7KB: replicatedState - one immutable structurally shared revision per change, callback failure rolling back and revoking escaped drafts, a PromiseLike callback rejected, nested changes refused without losing the outer rollback, and the source cursor contract.
18.1KB: regression tests for 10 resolved application requests, each numbered in its test name.
22.8KB: regression tests for a phase-1a review's findings #1-#11 plus the requested race tests, with fits()-based contract assertions.
5.3KB: the Durable Object driver against a node:sqlite stand-in - BLOB values as Uint8Array, get() reading only the cursor's first row, and a bigint outside the safe-integer range refused.
2.3KB: a stand-in for a SQLite-backed Durable Object's ctx.storage over node:sqlite, with the real value types (ArrayBuffer in and out) and a cursor reporting which operation was used.

4KB: the migration runner - independent histories per metadata table, applied migrations skipped, a stored version newer than supported refused, and invalid version sequences rejected before the database is touched.
7KB: the Node driver - the configured PRAGMA defaults, committing work done through the transaction handle, idempotent close, and serialisation of concurrent transactions.
10.3KB: the structural diff between cell revisions.

5KB: draft semantics - only changed branches copied, frozen bases with deletion and native array mutators, inserted values copied so they do not alias the caller's object, comparator edits kept during sort, and writes through detached child references dropped.
4.3KB: a seeded fuzz - 100 seeds x 100 steps, asserting the prepared base, the replica replayed from the ops, the adopted value and the alias-freedom of the result at every step.

8.1KB: init runs after the resources are open and before the object goes live, cannot be read inside the factory, fails the activation and closes its resources on throw (the next get retries), runs in a root so it can call other objects, and across a reload an existing cell is kept while an added cell runs init during prepare.
1.5KB: the value semantics of a cell.

8.8KB: the cells - snapshots then exact ops with derivations following, primitive cells and value-returning changes, a returned value failing the schema rejected even outside dev mode, initial values always validated, writes from inside a factory rejected as read_only, listeners in a fresh root and tasks with an abortable ctx, and re-entrant writes publishing in adoption order.
4KB: runs the SHARED telemetry-store conformance suite from packages/telemetry against both the Node and the Durable Object adapter.
14.8KB: runs the SHARED telemetry-adapter conformance suite from packages/telemetry/src/testing against the SQLite adapter, plus row-level assertions.

17.4KB: the tutorial's own test - reads docs/tutorial.md, extracts every example:name block, extracts the matching example:name/end-example:name block from the test source, normalises and compares them, and then runs the example, so docs cannot drift.
1.8KB: the type-level assertions.

6.1KB: variants - a new variant's members arrive with its shape, a member outside it throws not_in_variant, every shape is readable in full at the moment it is shown, and after a link loss the last values stay readable while one fresh unit is sent and a joining reference waits.

6.1KB: WebSocket links against a real ws server - a client is served and stamped by the authenticator, a peer announcing itself as a host is cut off, an unauthenticated socket is closed and the client's calls wait for a reconnect, large snapshots arrive as binary messages, inflateMessage converts them back, and a client's binary message closes the socket.
9-line build config extending the repo base; the package's sideEffects:false is what lets the bundler drop unused exports.
